title: Control plane partition caused by ENI reattach race during private node upgrade
creator: Jonas Meyer
description: During a rolling upgrade of private (VPC) nodes for a customer cluster, we observed a transient but repeatable control-plane partition. Several API requests failed and scheduled jobs were repeatedly retried. This ticket captures the incident summary, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and a prioritized list of action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-04T02:10Z - Upgrade batch start: rolling replacement of worker nodes in us-west-2a for customer-cluster-7.
2026-03-04T02:22Z - First node finished kubelet replacement; ENI detach/reattach logged by cloud provider and CNI.
2026-03-04T02:25Z - Control plane observed increased connection resets and recorded node heartbeats gap >30s; leader elections triggered for internal controllers.
2026-03-04T02:27Z - API errors spiked (5xx) and operator alerts fired; some LBs marked control plane endpoints unhealthy causing partial traffic routing to fallback region.
2026-03-04T02:40Z - Team paused upgrade and initiated incident response; mitigation: increased kube-apiserver gracePeriod and manually cordoned remaining nodes in batch.
2026-03-04T03:10Z - Hotfix PR created to add deterministic ordering to ENI detach/attach flow and add pre-detach connectivity probe to CNI plugin.
2026-03-04T08:00Z - Hotfix merged to canary channel; canary cluster upgrade completed without control plane partition for 2 canaries.
2026-03-04T12:00Z - Gradual rollout resumed with updated CNI; monitoring shows no further partitions.
impact_summary: Approximately 6 customer clusters experienced elevated control-plane error rates for ~15-35 minutes. API requests timed out or returned 500 during the window; automated jobs and scheduled tasks were delayed. No data loss was observed, but customer SLAs were degraded for the duration.
root_cause: A race condition between the cloud ENI reattachment lifecycle and the cluster CNI plugin's attach/detach handlers. When the cloud provider reassigned the ENI to a node there was a short window where the node's IP moved but the CNI did not complete its local networking reconciliation. This produced duplicate ARP/route state and transient packet loss to control-plane components. The node kubelet briefly reported NotReady which triggered controller churn and leader re-elections. The rolling upgrade's timing (parallel detaches within the same AZ) increased the likelihood of the race.
action_items: A1: Merge and backport CNI pre-detach connectivity probe (owner: Aisha Patel) - due 2026-03-16
A2: Update upgrade orchestration to serialize ENI detach across AZs when performing private upgrades (owner: Michael Chen) - due 2026-03-22
A3: Increase kube-apiserver heartbeat tolerance and add adaptive gracePeriod only during rolling upgrades (owner: Priya Rao) - due 2026-03-18
A4: Harden cloud provider retry logic for ENI attach/detach and surface clearer attach-state in logs (owner: Cloud SDK team) - due 2026-03-28
A5: Add end-to-end network validation step to upgrade runbook and automate pre-upgrade canary with synthetic control-plane calls (owner: SRE team) - due 2026-03-20
A6: Create an observability dashboard that correlates ENI attach events, node readiness, and control-plane error rates (owner: Observability team) - due 2026-03-17
A7: Run a cross-team drill and tabletop with Platform, SRE, and Private Deployments to validate new mitigations (owner: Platform PM - Elena Garcia) - due 2026-04-01
decisions: Decided to prioritize a software-side mitigation (CNI probe + serialize detach) over immediate infra changes to cloud provider configs because it provides fastest remediation path across all customers.
Opted for an adaptive kube-apiserver gracePeriod during upgrades rather than global increase to avoid masking real network failures in steady state.
Chosen rollout strategy: canary -> small cohort -> full resume, with automatic pause on control-plane error rate > 2x baseline.
notes: Progress: Hotfix merged to main and backported to 2026.03 release; canary verification completed for 2 clusters on 2026-03-04.
Blockers: Need cloud provider confirmation on delayed attach-state semantics for ENIs when host recovery spans AZ boundaries (ticket opened with provider).
Follow-ups: Observability dashboard work is in progress; preliminary panels available but needs correlation queries for ARP/route anomalies.
Communication plan: Postmortem email draft prepared; CS will notify affected customers with summary and planned mitigations once A1/A5 are complete.
